land_roll_terms: execution_quality (actor's combined_mastery blended with technique_stat, scaled by 0.6 + 0.4 * combined_mastery)
defense_factor includes the top man's base defense stat: clampf(defense/100 * 0.35 + bonus, 0.0, 0.6)
no DEFENSE_ANSWERS key answers the 'escape' class, so the technique bonus is always 0 against escapes
camp attack/defense bonuses and duel_edge success also apply
stand_up_roll_terms: execution_quality is the BOTTOM man's (the escaper's) execution quality from the landed escape
a single rng.randf() < escape_chance decides the stand-up
on success: phase -> STANDING, top_side cleared, range_band -> CLINCH
the top man's stats, defense, grapple and BJJ proficiency do NOT appear in this roll
top_man_terms: the top man IS present in the LAND roll: his defense stat sets the base defense_factor (defense/100 * 0.35) that the escape must beat
his mobility (_mobility_factor) scales the defense_factor multiplicatively
his camp sub_defense does NOT apply to escapes (it applies to submission finishes only)
the top man is ABSENT from the STAND-UP roll: escape_chance reads only the escaper's execution_quality
a high-grapple top man with strong defense makes it harder for the escape to LAND, but once it lands, his stats do not resist the stand-up

options.rule: The top man's control skill resists the stand-up roll: subtract a factor derived from the top man's grapple and BJJ proficiency from the escape_chance, so a dominant grappler on top makes it harder for the bottom man to stand up even after the escape lands.

A landed dominant position (side control, mount, back) sets a hold bonus that decays per exchange: the next escape must beat an additional threshold proportional to how many consecutive exchanges the top man has held the seat, making repeated ground work progressively harder to escape from.

A landed escape that fails to stand the top man up carries SUBMISSION_SWITCH_CARRY of the top man's pressure instead of zeroing it: the bottom man's failed stand-up attempt does not reset the submission threat, so repeated escape attempts accumulate pressure toward a finish rather than clearing it.
